label: Business or finance
blurb: Accounting, management, economics. You understand what a balance sheet is for.
outcome: You will be the man on every finance council for the rest of your life. Nothing academic gets cheaper for you, and free time in the philosophy years will be scarce. But when a parish is drowning, someone will remember what you studied.

label: Philosophy or theology
blurb: You read Aquinas before anyone told you to. You arrived with opinions.
outcome: The philosophy years will be a review, and you will bank more free time than any other man in the class. The faculty will assume you are orthodox and slightly dull; that assumption is yours to confirm or destroy. Your convictions are already forming, and they will move faster than other men's.

label: History or law
blurb: Documents, precedents, institutions and how they actually work.
outcome: You read a document properly, which in the Church is rarer than holiness. The canon law track is open to you from the start, and the tribunal and the chancellor's office are the strongest institutional careers in the game. Nobody will ever call you warm.

label: Science, engineering, or medicine
blurb: You are used to being right in a way that can be checked.
outcome: You will find the philosophy years harder than the theology men do, and you will say so. In exchange you have credibility with the skeptical, the technical, and the donors in medicine and tech, and a real competence with buildings and systems that most priests lack entirely.

label: Classics or English
blurb: Latin, Greek, the long sentence, the exact word.
outcome: The best homily curve in the game is yours if you work it. Latin and Greek will make later study cheap, and liturgical and translation work will find you. You will be assumed to be an aesthete, and the assumption will not be entirely wrong.

label: Education
blurb: A teaching degree: classroom management, child development, and a student-teaching semester that taught you what a room of the unwilling looks like.
outcome: You can hold a room and you know how a curriculum is built. Philosophy will be new to you, but not the discipline of learning it.

label: Nursing or allied health
blurb: Anatomy, clinical rotations, night shifts, and the particular calm of people who have seen blood.
outcome: You are not squeamish and you know how hospitals work, and that will matter more than anyone at the seminary expects, sooner than you think.

label: Psychology or social science
blurb: How people work, in the aggregate and one at a time. Statistics you will never use and interviews you will.
outcome: You listen better than most, and you know the names for what you hear. Some of the faculty will find that useful and some will find it suspicious.
